Assignment 03 / Sculpting for Design

Impressions of the Everyday

A memory of the sea, held in texture, relief, and blue.

Impressions · Plaster relief · Colour

For Medha, the beach is connected with family visits, college friendships, and moments of reflection. These relief pieces draw on that personal relationship with the water.

01

Returning to the water

During annual visits to her aunt’s home in Trivandrum, going to the beach was a must. Medha and her brother would spend hours playing in the water until their mother called them back. Later, the beach in Chennai became part of her college life too — a place to go and process both good and difficult moments.

She has also collected shells from her visits over time. The project draws from this accumulated familiarity with the coast: the movement of waves, the forms of marine life, and the feeling of looking out at the water.

02

Planning an underwater world

The initial sketches explore two formats: a rectangular composition and a circular one. Both organise marine forms within a bounded surface, testing how the surrounding water might connect the individual elements.

The drawings also note the role of texture. Rather than leaving the background flat, Medha planned for it to contribute to the feeling of the piece.

03

Making an impression

Medha pressed fabric over the mould to give the background a textured feel. This treatment suggests water moving around the other elements. Different tools were used to create the parts of the marine scene.

The unpainted relief makes those material decisions particularly visible: raised forms, repeated impressions, and winding lines sit within the same textured field. The painted version then gives each part a stronger visual identity.

04

Blue, green, and the movement between

Colour brings a new layer to the relief. Blue connects the surface into a single underwater space; green follows the long, curving plant forms; warmer colours distinguish other details from the water around them.

The circular piece develops the same marine theme in a more compact format. These two views show how its raised elements catch light and cast small shadows, keeping the tactile quality visible beneath the paint.

05

A familiar place, carried into a material

The work aims to capture something of the feeling Medha gets from staring into the waves. It combines a personal subject with a process in which everyday materials can leave lasting marks.

Her reflection on the assignment ends with a fitting consequence: making the pieces prompted her to plan another beach outing with friends.
